title: Two field extensions embed in a common field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension] and let $E/k$ and $F/k$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension]. Then there exists a field $M$ [def-pc-field-extension] and $k$-field embeddings $E\to M$ and $F\to M$.

proof.text: Regard $E$ and $F$ as $k$-algebras through their field-extension structures and put $T=E\otimes_kF$. The canonical factor maps $E\to T$ and $F\to T$ are injective by [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-tensor-inclusions].

source.place: Fields, Lemma 9.2, tag 0H7K (construction via tensor product)

proof.text: Since $E$ and $F$ are fields, they are domains, so [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-tensor-nontrivial] gives that $T$ is nontrivial.
Choose a maximal ideal $I$ of $T$ using [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-maximal-ideal], and set $M=T/I$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-quotient-field], $M$ is a field.

source.place: Fields, Lemma 9.2, tag 0H7K (take a residue field of the tensor product)

proof.text: The quotient map $T\to M$ composed with the two canonical factor maps gives $k$-algebra homomorphisms $E\to M$ and $F\to M$. Their kernels are ideals of the fields $E$ and $F$; each map sends $1$ to $1$, so its kernel is not the whole ring and therefore is zero. Hence these maps are $k$-field embeddings.

split_report.summary: Split the common-overfield lemma through the tensor product: the field factors inject into and make the tensor product nontrivial, a maximal ideal exists, and its quotient is a field; the induced unital maps from each factor are injective.
